issues.description: Method parameter type mismatch for Pneumatic.raisePressure: the UML in the problem statement specifies raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) (problem_statement.md lines 16-19), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) (solution src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 5) while the concrete classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (solution src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java line 10 and src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 10). This inconsistency (interface using double vs implementations using int and UML specifying int) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across UML, interface, template and implementations. Preferred fix: change the Pneumatic interface method to void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) in both the solution and the template (so it matches the UML and the current implementations). Alternatively, if double is intended, update the UML and all implementing classes to use double. After the change, recompile to ensure no signature mismatches remain.
